[00:00] Amira (Redwood): ok good afternoon everyone, thanks for joining, quick check — you all see the deck?
[00:08] Evan (NimbleCX): yep we're good, thanks Amira.
[00:10] Amira: great, today's goal : run through a staging cutover simulation, make sure our compatibility gate rules are clear and rehearse a hot swap/rollback path. Not a full run, more of a rehearsal and decide next steps. Matt you wanna kick off with the pin matrix?
[00:25] Matt (Redwood SE): sure, I'll share my screen in a sec, but the short version: we recommend a three-tier pinning approach — stable pin for prod routes, shadow pin for new variants, and a soft-fallback mapping to lower-capacity compatible variants. numbers we saw in the bench — for the 8k context workflow, p95 on the large-open model was ~210ms on our dedicated nodes, small quantized model p95 ~350ms but cost is lower.
[00:48] Maya (NimbleCX): sorry can you repeat the latency for the quantized model, I think I missed the 210 vs 350?
[00:54] Matt: yeah so the non quant path (the big fp16 variant) median ~95ms, p95 ~210. The q4_0-ish quantized variant was higher p95 in our microbench due to some kernel mismatch we haven't optimized yet, so p95 bumped to ~350 in that run, but cost per token dropped ~45%.
[01:16] Rahul (NimbleCX): that's interesting — our SLA for customer-facing chat needs p95 < 300ms. So the quant variant might be borderline for our most latency-sensitive route.
[01:26] Sofia (Redwood): that aligns with our suggestion: pin the main chat route to the non-quant stable variant for now, and use quantized as soft-fallback for batch and lower-priority requests. Also we can enable prefix/KV caching to shave tokens off and reduce tail latency.
[01:44] Evan: quick Q on fallback — if the main model is overloaded, will requests automatically route to a fallback variant with the same API shape? we need to ensure function-calling and output schema stay consistent.
[01:55] Matt: good call. We support policy-based routing — yes we can route only to model variants that pass compatibility checks. The gating process verifies the function signature and sample outputs; if mismatch, it won't auto-fallback unless you opt in for a tolerant mapping.
[02:10] Leah (NimbleCX): and where does the gating run? in our staging or Redwood's test harness?
[02:17] Matt: gating is a hybrid — we run unit compatibility checks in Redwood CI, but for actual behavioral regression tests we recommend running your golden prompts in staging so you get real KV/cache behavior and load effects.
[02:28] Maya: that's key for us — a number of our failure modes were due to tokenization edge cases and long-kv interactions, not just raw logits differences.
[02:37] Amira: ok let's table the nitty-gritty, plan for: NimbleCX to supply 10k prompt set + golden outputs, Redwood to run a 2-hour staging load with the pinned matrix. If the gate fails we follow the rollback playbook.
[02:51] Evan: can you quickly walk through the rollback playbook? last time it felt a bit hand-wavy.
[02:58] Matt: absolutely. The rollback playbook is: 1) detect via anomaly alert (latency/error SLO breach) 2) trigger automatic model-rule freeze (writes to the version gateway) 3) attempt a fast soft-swap to pre-approved fallback variant, 4) if soft-swap fails or compatibility mismatches occur, initiate circuit-breaker which routes to the previous stable pinned variant and throttle traffic while ops investigates. We instrument audit events for each step.
[03:28] Rahul: how long is the propagation window for a model-route swap? we have concerns about sticky sessions and cached contexts.
[03:36] Sofia: by default it's near-instant at the API layer (few seconds), but KV and client-side caches can create residual sessions. We recommend a short TTL for session caches during cutover (e.g., 30s) and a rolling drain window across pods to minimize tail impacts.
[03:50] Maya: do you have a preflight test to validate session stickiness before cutover?
[03:55] Matt: yes, our staging harness supports a session-ttl sweep and will surface mismatches. We'll include that in the 2-hour run.
[04:02] Speaker 1: [inaudible]... latency spike at 3:40?
[04:05] Amira: sorry I think that was noise, ok next — security and compliance. Evan, Leah, what are your must-haves?
[04:12] Leah: SOC2 excerpts were useful but we need KMS integration (customer-managed keys) and confirmation of audit-log retention policy for the Dedicated environment. Also SSO/SAML metadata for our admin users.
[04:24] Amira: we can support customer-managed keys and provide audit log exports. For Dedicated we map to your KMS during setup. I'll send the security addendum and a short note on retention windows.
[04:35] Evan: also need VPC peering details — can you accept a cross-account peering or do we use private endpoints?
[04:42] Sofia: both options exist; for air-gapped we offer on-prem package but for your case VPC peering + private endpoints is standard. Rahul, you'll want the peering guide we published, it has the CIDR and port list.
[04:54] Rahul: sweet. I'll look at that after this call.
[04:58] Amira: ok back to the simulation specifics — Matt, what's in the pinned matrix you're proposing for the run?
[05:05] Matt: I'm proposing: route A (live chat) -> pinned v2026-03-stable (fp16) ; shadow v2026-04-experiment (quant) ; fallback map -> v2026-02-compat (smaller architecture). Route B (batch Insights) -> pinned quant variant; fallback -> even smaller quant. We'll attach a CSV with exact model tags and hash ids after the call.
[05:26] Maya: will the shadow traffic run inline or via split? we need to capture outputs for eval without impacting p95.
[05:33] Sofia: shadow via split, no impact on production p95; storage of shadow responses goes to a secure S3 bucket and is tagged for eval.
[05:40] Evan: one operational question — can you simulate a partial region failure? we want to see cross-region fallback to our DR region.
[05:48] Matt: yes we can simulate region failover in staging by toggling routing policy; we recommend doing a separate DR tabletop, but we can inject a regional failover in the 2-hour run if you want.
[05:58] Rahul: please do, we want to validate session continuity and KV cache misses under region fail.
[06:03] Amira: noted, add region failover injection to the run.
[06:07] Speaker 2 (Customer): um, is there an expected cost uplift for enabling shadowing and retaining full shadow outputs?
[06:14] Amira: yes modest uplift — shadowing is billed for tokens written and storage for the shadow corpus; we'll share an estimate after Matt defines rates for the run. The Optimize tool can project per-hour costs.
[06:25] Leah: on the compatibility tests, what passes vs fails? is it strict schema equality?
[06:30] Matt: compatibility tiers: strict (signature + function call presence + exact required fields), tolerant (allow missing optional fields if a mapping exists), semantic (compare embedding or output similarity above threshold). Only strict passes automatic fallback; tolerant requires manual sign-off.
[06:46] Maya: for our user messages we need function calling exactness so strict gate for those routes.
[06:51] Amira: ok we'll mark chat route as strict in the pin matrix.
[06:55] Matt: also note we have model quantization quirks that can change tokenization for rare chars — we'll run tokenizer diff tests as part of compatibility.
[07:06] Evan: we've had a couple of prompts where punctuation shifted meaning — it's these tokenizer diffs that bit us in the prod pilot last quarter.
[07:13] Sofia: yup, that's why we asked for the golden outputs. We'll run a token-level diff and surface mismatches.
[07:19] Rahul: what about monitoring and alerting thresholds — can we tune the anomaly detectors for we've only minor blips?
[07:26] Matt: yes, detectors are configurable. Suggest starting with 2x baseline on error rate and 1.5x on p95 as soft alert. Thresholds can be tuned after the first run.
[07:36] Amira: let's talk about the tabletop rollback drill scope — quick sim, we want to exercise detection, auto-swap, and manual revert. Estimated 30-45 minutes. Who from NimbleCX should be present?
[07:47] Evan: Maya and Rahul for sure, Leah as decision owner, maybe one engineer from infra.
[07:53] Amira: perfect. We'll propose dates in the week of 2026-04-13.
[07:58] Speaker 3: [crosstalk]... can you also show the audit trail?
[08:02] Matt: yep audit trail is captured, each route change writes an event with user id, timestamp, previous/pinned versions, and propagation status. We'll share a sample event log.
[08:13] Maya: when you say 'fast soft-swap' can we pre-authorize a set of fallbacks so the API can choose without manual approval?
[08:21] Sofia: yes that is the pre-approved fallback list in the pin matrix — we can set which models are eligible for automatic swap. For anything outside that list it'll require manual approval.
[08:31] Leah: ops question — in Dedicated, who has access to change pinned versions? we need RBAC controls.
[08:36] Amira: RBAC exists; you can assign admin/change rights to a small group. We'll document the roles and map to SSO groups you provide.
[08:45] Evan: there was a note about an inconsistency in the earlier benchmark doc — Matt, can you confirm the p95 numbers across region variants?
[08:54] Matt: I'll run a short cross-region microbench and update the spreadsheet; there was a small measuring difference because one run had caching warm. We'll re-run cold and warm tests.
[09:04] Maya: do we need to do a full retrain or model patch if a semantic regression is found?
[09:10] Matt: usually no — for small semantic regressions we prefer prompt-level mitigations or dynamic post-processing; retrain is a heavy lift and rare.
[09:18] Rahul: understood. For the load test, can we include a synthetic mix that matches our prod–80/10/10 percentage of long, medium, short contexts?
[09:26] Sofia: yes include that in the config — we'll take your traffic profile.

[09:36] Evan: we're ok.

[09:50] Leah: can you also include a short runbook for manual rollback steps we can store in our runbook repo?
[09:56] Amira: yes we'll draft a 1-page runbook.
[09:59] Maya: last thing — can you log the expected cost delta for enabling the shadowing + region failover tests? just a ballpark.
[10:07] Matt: ballpark we'll estimate and send with the run plan.
